tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start with the README and documentation hub to understand what Nxus is: a local-first application manager and productivity hub built as an Nx monorepo. The README introduces the six mini-apps (Gateway, Core, Workbench, Calendar, Editor, Recall), their port assignments, and the overall architecture. The architecture overview provides a deeper look at the tech stack — TanStack Start, SQLite, Tailwind/Radix UI — and the hybrid browser-plus-local-server system that bridges sandboxed browser UI with native OS operations via server functions.

tour.title: Monorepo Foundation
tour.description: The project's skeleton is defined by its workspace configuration. The Nx config orchestrates builds across all apps and libs using the @nx/js/typescript plugin. The pnpm workspace YAML declares apps/*, libs/*, and packages/* as workspace packages, while the root package.json defines the dev, test, lint, and e2e scripts that drive day-to-day development. The base TypeScript config enforces strict mode, ES2022 target, and bundler module resolution across the entire monorepo.
tour.languageLesson: Nx monorepos use project-level tsconfig files that extend a base config. The 'composite: true' setting enables TypeScript project references for incremental builds across workspace packages.

tour.title: Gateway Landing Page
tour.description: The Gateway (port 3001) is the user's first touchpoint — a landing page that lists all mini-apps and acts as a reverse proxy. The route index renders mini-app cards with a switchable visual style system offering 11 presentation modes (glass 3D, terminal, orbital, etc.), persisting the user's preference to localStorage. The mini-apps config is a central registry of all five sub-applications with their IDs, display names, descriptions, icons, and route paths. The root layout provides the HTML shell, QueryClient, and theme initialization with FOUC prevention.
tour.languageLesson: TanStack Router uses file-based routing — each file in routes/ becomes a URL path. The __root.tsx provides the layout wrapper, while index.tsx handles the '/' route. Route trees are auto-generated into routeTree.gen.ts for type-safe navigation.

tour.title: Core App & Command System
tour.description: Core (port 3000) is the main application, handling app management, command palette, inbox, and settings. Its router mounts at /core with TanStack Router and file-based routes. The command palette registry aggregates app-bound commands and global generic commands (settings, inbox, AI operations, DB tools) with alias-based search prioritization. The command execution module routes commands through a params modal when they require user input. The PTY session manager provides server-side pseudo-terminal sessions for running local commands with output buffering and lifecycle management.
tour.languageLesson: Files ending in .server.ts contain TanStack Start server functions that run only on the Node.js server. This is how the browser UI accesses local OS operations (file system, shell, databases) through a thin RPC layer without needing a separate API server.

tour.title: Node-Based Data Model
tour.description: The entire system is built on a Tana-inspired 'everything is a node' architecture. The data model documentation explains how nodes have IDs, names, properties, and supertags — a functional type system with inheritance and behavioral mapping. Core supertags like #app, #command, #remote-repo, and #category define what nodes can do. The nxus-db types barrel re-exports the full type vocabulary (items, workflows, commands, queries, nodes, recall), while the schemas barrel defines the database shape. The node service is the CRUD and query layer providing cached lookups, supertag inheritance, property management, and node assembly.

tour.title: Graph Database & Query Engine
tour.description: Building on the node data model from Step 5, the graph client connects to SurrealDB in three modes — embedded file, remote server, or in-memory — and bootstraps core tables (node, supertag, relations) with system supertags. The core graph service adds semantic operations: 6 relation types, Tana-style recursive traversals (componentsRec, dependenciesRec, ancestorsRec), full-text search, and polling-based live query subscriptions. The query evaluator engine takes QueryDefinition filters (supertag, property, content, temporal, relation, logical) and evaluates them against the node database, returning sorted and paginated AssembledNode results.

tour.title: Reactive Query System
tour.description: The reactive module brings the node database to life with smart change propagation. The dependency tracker maps query-to-field dependencies, analyzing query definitions to extract field, supertag, and content dependencies. When a mutation occurs, only the affected subscriptions are re-evaluated — avoiding expensive brute-force re-queries. The reactive barrel exports the full toolkit: event bus, query subscription service, automation service, computed field service, webhook queue, and performance metrics. This is the engine that keeps every UI component in sync with the underlying data.

tour.title: Shared UI & Design System
tour.description: The nxus-ui library provides the shared UI foundation — most notably the cn() utility combining clsx conditional class names with tailwind-merge for Tailwind CSS conflict resolution, used across every component in every app (18 imports, highest fan-in). The core app's root stylesheet configures the full design token system for light/dark modes via Tailwind + shadcn integration. The theme-imports barrel pulls in 21 theme stylesheets organized into core themes (tokyonight, dracula, nord), wild themes (synthwave, gruvbox, rosepine), and expressive themes (anime, cyberpunk, brutalism).
tour.languageLesson: The cn() pattern — cn(clsx(...), tailwindMerge) — is the standard approach in shadcn/ui codebases. It allows conditional class composition while automatically resolving Tailwind conflicts like 'px-4 px-2' to just 'px-2'.

tour.title: Outline Editor
tour.description: The Editor (port 3004) implements a Tana-like outline editor. The primary OutlineEditor component renders the hierarchical node tree with breadcrumbs, field sections, backlinks, and a command palette, orchestrating data loading and a Zustand store. Each node renders through NodeBlock, which manages the full pipeline: bullet display, content editing, field sections, query results, and view mode switching (table, kanban, cards, list). The Bullet component provides expand/collapse toggles with supertag color indicators and child count badges, while SupertagPill renders colored type badges using a deterministic DJB2 hash color assignment when no explicit color is set.

tour.title: Graph Workbench
tour.description: The Workbench (port 3002) provides node browsing, graph visualization, and a query builder — the power-user interface for the node database from Steps 5-6. The graph store (highest fan-in in the workbench library, 13 imports) manages physics, display, filter, and view options through Zustand. The graph types define renderer-agnostic interfaces (GraphNode, GraphEdge, GraphData) consumed by both 2D and 3D renderers. The edge extractor system runs four extractors (dependency, backlink, reference, hierarchy) with deduplication to produce the visual graph. The use-query hook provides the TanStack Query data-fetching layer with automatic cache invalidation — the highest fan-out file in the project (23 imports).

tour.title: Calendar & Google Sync
tour.description: The Calendar app (port 3003) manages events with Google Calendar synchronization. The Google Calendar client handles OAuth2 authentication, token management, event CRUD, batch sync, and error handling using the googleapis package. The event mutation hooks provide optimistic updates and TanStack Query cache invalidation for seamless CRUD operations. Together they implement a two-way sync: local changes push to Google, while batch sync pulls remote events — all built on the same node architecture from Step 5.

tour.title: Recall & AI Agents
tour.description: Recall (port 3005) implements spaced repetition learning with AI-powered concept extraction. The review session route drives the core UX: displaying due cards with question/answer flow, session timing, and FSRS-based rating. The nxus-mastra agents barrel exports AI functions — generateConcepts, generateQuestion, evaluateAnswer, explainFurther, extractConceptsFromText — along with a client facade and Bloom's taxonomy progression logic. This is the only app that integrates LLM-powered intelligence, turning raw content into structured learning material.

tour.title: Testing & CI Pipeline
tour.description: The E2E test suite covers all six apps with Playwright. The gateway spec verifies app card rendering and navigation to each sub-application. The core specs cover the gallery, command palette, inbox, and settings. Editor tests exercise node creation, editing, indentation, and supertag references. Workbench tests cover graph view, node browser, and query builder. The CI pipeline runs three parallel jobs on every PR: linting, unit tests with coverage, and Playwright E2E tests across matrix variants — ensuring the entire multi-app ecosystem works together.
tour.languageLesson: Playwright's base fixture pattern (extending the default test object with custom helpers like navigateToApp) lets you share retry logic and navigation utilities across all test suites without duplicating setup code.
